summary: Independent recheck of T75's repair of T70 F-001..F-004 on branch codex/agent-first-core at base 0bc6418. Stage 1 rows 2, 3 and 4 PASS under my own execution; row 1 FAILS. T75's own delta is verified accurate in every case: the corrected cli-reference.md/modules.md exit-behaviour paragraph holds against 19 measured cells including check-output (a surface neither T70's nor T75's own probe exercised); the F-002 closed vocabulary (safeValidationError/KNOWN_VALIDATION_ERRORS) resists every escape attempted (case, whitespace, prefix, empty, undefined, long no-substring string) while known-safe strings survive unchanged; the F-003 manifest sentence matches self-protect.ts's real behaviour (exactly one findings.push, the checksum arm); the two new F-004/F-004-F-002 regressions genuinely drive the real runAdapter->computeGate->writeOutputs pipeline, read the persisted artifact back from disk, and re-read the gate through the real service - proven, not assumed, to be load-bearing by a probe that manually constructs a leaking SourceRunInfo and shows the same downstream pipeline propagates it faithfully (i.e. the shipped assertions would fail if the producer's fix regressed). Row 1 fails because a from-scratch re-enumeration, extended to src/lib/templates.ts - a shipped-guidance surface none of T62/T68/T70/T73/T75 ever swept - finds two new defects: the generated git pre-push hook script (written verbatim into every scaffolded project's .git/hooks/pre-push by keryx init/update) still enumerates blocking modes as enforced/ci, omitting gateway, in two shell comments; and docs/docs/modules.md's CLI-surface table mislabels both security scan-mcp and security hooks install|uninstall's Exit column 'mode-gated' when both are measured to be gated by something else entirely (--strict for scan-mcp, pure runtime/settings validation for hooks) - never by config.mode. The scan-mcp mislabel is reachable in the exact 'a check that did not pass looks like a pass' shape this phase exists to close: a CI job that sets mode:ci believing that alone gates scan-mcp on MCP threats never fails unless --strict is also passed. A fourth, lower-severity finding notes four shipped sites narrow the pre-push block condition to 'a secret/critical finding' when resolve.ts's computeGate actually gates on any category's block action, severity>=failOn, or require-approval action - the opposite (understating) direction. Also independently reproduced the mock.module cross-file hazard both T69 and T75 report (byte-for-byte identical provenance.test.ts failure, in the file order that matters), confirmed the shipped mock-free design is clean against it in both orders, and ruled the two test-only exports (runAdapter, writeOutputs) an acceptable price on the same terms T70 already applied to the first one - zero production blast radius for both, a hazard now independently confirmed rather than taken on faith, and full coverage of the specific claim under test. No production, test, or documentation file was modified; file hashes are identical start to end for every file this review or the concurrent exfil.ts/policies.md reviewer touched.

findings.problem: The git pre-push hook script this function generates -- written verbatim into every scaffolded project's .git/hooks/pre-push by keryx init/update -- carries two shell comments enumerating which security.config.json modes block a push ('enforced'/'ci' exit non-zero...; # enforced/ci mode blocked on this file.) that omit `gateway`, even though gateway has blocked identically to enforced/ci since T61/T65. This is the same defect class T62/T68/T70/T73/T75 corrected at eighteen other sites, in a nineteenth site (src/lib/templates.ts) none of those five prior rounds' surface sweeps ever included.
findings.impact: AC8's 'no shipped guidance describes behaviour the code does not have' fails on a surface as durable as the manifest/README the module already ships -- a git hook persists on disk and is not re-read the way a markdown doc is. An operator or agent reading their own .git/hooks/pre-push to understand gateway-mode behaviour is told only enforced/ci matter, the exact 'gateway mode is inert' misreading this phase exists to close.
findings.suggested_fix: Add gateway to both comments, matching src/security/templates.ts:63's already-corrected wording ('enforced'/'ci'/'gateway' block the push). Add a pinning regression for renderSecurityPrePushHook()'s own output, matching the pattern templates.test.ts already uses for renderSecurityManifest/renderSecurityCoreReadme.

findings.problem: modules.md's CLI-surface table marks security scan-mcp's Exit column 'mode-gated', and the paragraph immediately below (:784-787) states that mode-gated commands honor config.mode with the advisory/enforced-ci-gateway fold. handleScanMcp (src/commands/security.ts:384-536) never calls modeOf(cwd) and never reads config.mode; its only exit-affecting line gates on `--strict` and (totalFindings>0 || coverage==='incomplete') alone.
findings.impact: Reachable 'a check that did not pass looks like a pass' gap: a CI job that sets mode:'ci' believing that alone makes security scan-mcp gate on MCP threats (as the doc implies for every 'mode-gated' row) never fails on any MCP threat in any mode unless --strict is also passed -- silently passing a poisoned MCP manifest through CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the scan-mcp row's Exit column to '1 with --strict, on a threat or incomplete coverage (independent of mode)' and scope the :784-787 paragraph explicitly to the rows it actually describes (scan, check-input, check-output, report).

findings.problem: Four shipped sites (.metaproject/modules/security.md:49, src/security/templates.ts:64, src/commands/init.ts:497, src/lib/templates.ts:2064) describe the pre-push block condition as 'a secret/critical finding'. resolve.ts:132-161's computeGate returns 'fail' on any category's block action or severity>=failOn (not specifically secret), and 'needs-approval' (which also exits non-zero in a blocking mode) on any category's require-approval action, e.g. escalated prompt-injection.
findings.impact: Opposite direction from F-001/F-002: undersells the blocking surface rather than oversells it, so the risk is operator surprise at an unexpected block, not a security bypass. Recorded under AC8's 'either direction' mandate; not blocking.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the category/severity qualifier: 'blocks the push (non-zero exit) on a failing or needs-approval gate', or give a non-exhaustive example ('e.g. a secret, PII or escalated prompt-injection finding').
